answer: Those are glossary terms. Once an article has a Glossary, the words it uses in a non-obvious way are underlined with orange dots in every mode, not just in the Glossary panel. Point at one to read its definition from the piece itself. Click **Open glossary** on that card for the full entry. See [Glossary](/help/mode-glossary) for how the list is made and how to add a term that is missing.

There are two ways, both under **Access & sharing** on the article's Metadata page.

- **A private link** is for the people you send it to. Press **Create a link**, tick that you have the right to share the text, and press **Create the link**, then copy and send it. Anyone with the link can read the article without an account, but it isn't listed anywhere, and they can't write or start any AI work. **Turn off** stops the link working.
- **Making it public** lists the article on [Shared articles](/read/public) for anyone to find. Press **Share with anyone…**, tick the same confirmation, and press **Share it**.

Visitors can read the article and the reading aids already made for it, plus your comments and bookmarks, but not your chats or your profile. See [Sharing](/help/sharing).

Skim is a mode for going round a paper more than once, a little deeper each time. It walks you through a route of stops, and each stop is one of the author's own sentences shown in place in the article, with a short cue telling you what to look for. Nothing is summarised for you: the stops come from the piece's Quotes and key Ideas, and the route is planned around what you said you want from the article.

Use **‹** and **›** at the top, or the arrow keys while reading, to step from stop to stop. **Gist** is a handful of stops, **More** about a dozen, and **Most** a larger share of the piece. Each pass goes a little deeper, and small dots under each stop's number show which passes it belongs to. Only whoever added the article can plan a route. See [Skim](/help/mode-skim).

No. Your allowance counts the articles you add. Opening modes, generating them, chatting, and re-running them are all included. The only other thing that counts is switching an article to High-powered AI. See [Plans](/help/plans).

Summary normally writes itself the first time you open it, which can take a minute or more on a long article. Keep a Spideryarn tab open while it works, since the work pauses if every tab is closed. Once it's written, it's stored, so reopening Summary is instant.

If it still doesn't appear, the Brief and Fuller buttons at the top of the panel are the things to check. On your own article it starts by itself, but if you arrived by a link or with Back, you'll see an empty panel with a button to start it. Press that button.

If nothing happens after several minutes, send [Feedback](/help/feedback) from the article so the team can look at it.

That's the **viewport marker** on the spine, the thin strip down the left edge of the reading view. It's the box with orange top and bottom edges, and it shows what's on your screen right now. It moves as you scroll, and its height tells you how much of the article fits on one screen. See [Reading the spine](/help/spine).

Yes. Your notes and comments are part of an article's export. On an article's Metadata page, **Export this article** downloads a zip of everything we hold for it, including your comments and bookmarks, as plain files you can open without Spideryarn. The original page or PDF and the images are not included. See [Your data: export, archive, delete](/help/your-data).

Your chats and your profile are not part of the shared-article view, but the export is the place to get your own marks out.

Yes, it works on phones and tablets, but it's designed for a large screen, so a few things behave differently. On a narrow screen a mode's panel covers the article instead of sitting beside it, and **Plain** gets you back to the text. Tapping twice on the spine or a link lets you see where it goes before you follow it, and pressing and holding selects words. On a home screen there's no Back button, so use the **↩ back to …** button above the bottom bar. The full details are on the [Phones and tablets](/help/touch) page.

Summary restates the piece in plain words, in **Brief** or **Fuller** lengths, or as a **Thread** of short posts; each paragraph links to the passages it rests on. Skim is a route through the article's Quotes and key Ideas, with each stop showing the author's own sentence in place and a cue for what to look for. Use Summary to decide whether a piece is worth your time, and Skim to go round a paper more than once, a little deeper each time. See [Summary](/help/mode-summary) and [Skim](/help/mode-skim).

The Help pages don't cover EPUB files or Kindle books, so I can't confirm whether Spideryarn accepts them. What they do cover is adding articles from a web address or from a file: a PDF, or a web page you saved as HTML. If you have a Kindle book you want to read, the nearest route is to use one of those formats if you have one (see [Adding an article](/help/adding-articles)). For a question about EPUB support, the [Feedback](/help/feedback) button sends it to the people who make Spideryarn.

The Help pages don't mention a student discount, so I can't say whether one exists. The plan details and allowance rules are on [Plans](/help/plans), and the current prices are on the pricing page. If you want to ask about a discount, use the **Feedback** button, which sends your question to the people who make Spideryarn.

I don't see anything in the Help pages about two people annotating the same article at the same time, so I can't confirm that it's supported. What the pages do say is that sharing lets others read an article and see your comments and bookmarks, but visitors cannot write anything. See [Sharing](/help/sharing) and [Comments and bookmarks](/help/comments). If you need live co-annotation, send the question through [Feedback](/help/feedback).

I don't see anything in the Help pages about an API or about driving Spideryarn from scripts, so I can't tell you whether one exists or how it would work. The closest things covered are the command bar, which takes typed or spoken commands inside an article ([Keyboard shortcuts](/help/keyboard)), and the bookmarklet that adds a page from its address ([Adding an article](/help/adding-articles)).

If you need scripted access, send the question through [Feedback](/help/feedback), which goes to the people who make Spideryarn.
